newsitem.title: UK: British home repossessions fall in second half 1996.
newsitem.headline: British home repossessions fall in second half 1996.

text.p: Home repossessions by mortgage lenders in Britain fell during the second half of 1996, the Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML) said on Wednesday.

At 18,460 the number of repossessions was over 23 percent lower than in the first half of the year. The figure was also the lowest since the first half of 1990 and "less than half the peak figure of 38,930 in the second half of 1991," it said.

The council said there had also been a marked improvement in the level of arrears and a fall in the stock of properties in possession. This was due to "a mixture of general improvement in the economy and the labour market", it added.

Michael Coogan, the CML's director general, said mortgage lenders were aware that levels of arrears and repossessions were well above those of the 1980s but the "nature of the employment market - with more contract working and less long-term security" might make a return to these levels difficult.

Coogan said the fall during the second half of 1996 reflected falls in unemployment and the effect of low interest rates. Arrears management techniques were having an influence and some borrowers were able to trade out of difficulty thanks to rising house prices, he added.

But higher interest rates, particularly if combined with any further reduction in mortgage interest tax relief or income support for mortgage interest, "could slow the improvement in arrears and possessions", Coogan said.
